title: PT Forisa Nusapersada
description:
# PT Forisa Nusapersada

**Industry:** Food & Beverage Manufacturing (FMCG)
**Headquarters:** Jakarta, Indonesia
**Manufacturing:** Cikupa (Tangerang) & Ungaran (Central Java)
**Revenue:** IDR 5.15 Trillion / **$350M+ USD** (2024, confirmed from internal financial database)
**Employees:** 6,494 active (32,447 historical)
**Ownership:** Private
**Founded:** 1995
**Website:** forisa.co.id
**Auditor:** PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC)

---

## Summary

PT Forisa Nusapersada is one of Indonesia's largest powder beverage and food manufacturers, operating since 1995. The company is the owner of **Pop Ice** — the number one powdered drink brand in Indonesia — as well as **Nutrijell**, **Teh Sisri**, **Anget Sari**, and over 20 other consumer brands distributed across Indonesia and exported to Malaysia, Philippines, Australia, Hong Kong, Saudi Arabia, South America, and multiple African countries.

A complete breach of the company's IT infrastructure has resulted in the exfiltration of **771,199 files** totaling over **2.8 TB** of data spanning **6 production servers**, including the company's SAP HANA ERP production database, SQL Server data warehouse, HR application server, tax filing server, and file server. **Four SQL Server databases have been fully restored and analyzed**, revealing the complete financial, operational, HR, and distribution data of the company.

Despite attempts to establish contact, the company has not responded.

---

## Scope of Compromised Data

**Total volume:** 771,199 files
**Data size:** 2.8 TB
**Coverage:** 6 internal servers, full SAP ERP, 4 SQL databases restored

### Infrastructure Compromised

| Server | Type | Data |
|--------|------|------|
| **FNPDATACIKUPA02** | NAS / File Server (Synology) | 209,634 files — 26 departments including Accounting, HR, IT, QA, R&D, Production |
| **FNPDATACKP01** | Backup Staging Server | 559,662 files — Tier1/Tier2 backups + Wasabi S3 cloud staging |
| **FNPDBPRD01** | SAP HANA Production Database | 584 GB full backup + restore kit with credentials |
| **FNPDBWH01** | SQL Server Data Warehouse | 192 GB — 7 databases (Financial, HR, Lab, Production, Reseller) |
| **FNPHRAPP01** | HR Application Server (Laravel) | ~310 GB / 2.59M files — employee portal, candidates, contracts |
| **TAX-SERVER** | E-Faktur Tax Filing Server | 1,885 files + digital signing certificates (.p12) |

### Active Directory Domain
- **Domain:** FORISA (forisa.co.id)
- **Domain Controller:** FNPDC01
- **Endpoints enumerated:** 268 devices (from Kaspersky Security Center report)

### Data Categories

| Category | Description |
|---|---|
| **Financial** | 430,727 sales invoices (2017-2026), IDR 5.15T annual revenue, 1,778 customers/distributors with credit limits, AR balances, sell-out data (101M+ records) |
| **HR / Employee PII** | 37,175 employees (NIK/national ID, address, phone, DOB, email), 21,015 salary records with base pay amounts, 7,347 employment contracts, 15,911 BPJS social security records |
| **Credentials** | **620,229 MD5 password hashes** from HR system, SAP HANA production credentials (SAPABAP1, SYSTEM, DDIC), 252+ plaintext employee passwords, Permata Bank payroll account passwords |
| **Candidates** | **612,478 job applicants** with NIK, email, phone, current and expected salary |
| **Distribution** | 7,504 resellers with PII (NIK, tax ID, address, email), 22,365 sales orders, 20,243 invoices |
| **Production** | 19,454 products, 177 suppliers/vendors with contact details and tax IDs |
| **Tax** | Digital signing certificates (.p12) for E-Faktur tax filing, Derby tax databases |
| **IT Audit** | PricewaterhouseCoopers ITGC/Cyber audit reports (2024-2025), SAP user access reviews with password hashes, sudoers configurations, server specifications |
| **Cloud** | Wasabi S3 access credentials (ap-southeast-1), rclone staging scripts |

---

## Key Financial Figures

| Year | Invoices | Revenue (IDR) | Revenue (USD) |
|------|----------|---------------|---------------|
| 2020 | 40,279 | IDR 3.95 Trillion | $274M |
| 2021 | 43,647 | IDR 4.11 Trillion | $285M |
| 2022 | 52,122 | IDR 4.64 Trillion | $324M |
| 2023 | 49,768 | IDR 4.88 Trillion | $341M |
| **2024** | **56,148** | **IDR 5.15 Trillion** | **$360M** |
| **2025** | **52,133** | **IDR 5.06 Trillion** | **$354M** |
| 2026 (Jan-Sep) | 38,301 | IDR 3.81 Trillion | $266M |

*Source: T_SLS_INV table from FNDB financial database, verified invoices only*

Revenue has grown consistently from IDR 2.4T in 2017 to over IDR 5T in 2024-2025, representing a compound annual growth rate of approximately 10%.

**Monthly payroll (September 2026):** IDR 3.42 Billion (~$216,000) for Cikupa factory alone via Permata Bank.

---

## Personal Data Exposed

| Category | Count | Details |
|----------|-------|---------|
| **Employee PII** | **37,175** | Full name, NIK (national ID), address, phone, DOB, position, department |
| **Job Candidates** | **612,478** | Full name, NIK, email, phone, salary history |
| **Credential Pairs** | **620,229** | Email + MD5 password hash |
| **Plaintext Passwords** | **252+** | Employee payslip passwords stored in Excel files |
| **BPJS Records** | **15,911** | Social security numbers, dependents' names |
| **Bank Account Data** | **1,600+** | Permata Bank payroll account numbers + passwords |
| **Reseller PII** | **7,504** | NIK, tax ID, address, email, phone |
| **Customer/Distributor** | **1,778** | Company details, credit limits, tax IDs |
| **Total unique individuals** | **~650,000+** | |

---

## Key Findings

- **SAP HANA production credentials exposed in plaintext** — database administrator accounts (SAPABAP1, SYSTEM, DDIC) found in a restore kit stored alongside the 584 GB database backup, enabling full access to the company's core ERP system
- **620,229 MD5 password hashes** — the company's HR system stores user passwords using the obsolete and trivially crackable MD5 algorithm with no salting
- **Bank payroll passwords follow a predictable pattern** — Permata Bank payroll account passwords use the format `Permata{MM}{YYYY}` (e.g., Permata062026), sent via unencrypted email and stored in .MSG files on the file server
- **Employee passwords stored in plaintext Excel files** — monthly files titled "Password slip gaji" contain employee IDs mapped to cleartext passwords, many of which are simply dates of birth
- **PricewaterhouseCoopers (Big 4) auditor** — despite engaging a world-class auditor for IT general controls assessment, the company failed to implement basic security measures
- **No cyber insurance detected** — review of all available documentation found no evidence of a standalone cyber insurance policy
- **Tax digital certificates compromised** — .p12 signing certificates for the Indonesian E-Faktur system were obtained, potentially enabling fraudulent tax filings
- **Cloud storage credentials exposed** — Wasabi S3 bucket access keys found in rclone scripts, providing access to the company's cloud data staging environment

---

## Consequences of Non-Cooperation

### Regulatory Exposure (Indonesia)
- **UU PDP (Law No. 27/2022 — Personal Data Protection):** Effective October 2024. Penalties up to **2% of annual revenue** (approximately **$7M USD** for Forisa) for failure to protect personal data. The breach affects 650,000+ individuals.
- **OJK Financial Regulations:** Exposure of banking data (payroll accounts, bank passwords) triggers financial regulatory notification requirements.
- **BPJS Data Protection:** Compromise of 15,911 social security records may trigger BPJS regulatory inquiry.

### Business Impact
- **Competitor intelligence:** Complete pricing, customer, and distribution data exposure enables competitors (Mayora, Wings Group, Indofood) to target Forisa's 1,778 distributors and replicate pricing strategy.
- **Brand damage:** Pop Ice and Nutrijell are household brands in Indonesia. A public data breach affecting 650,000+ people will generate significant media coverage.
- **SAP system integrity:** With exposed ERP credentials, the company cannot trust the integrity of its financial data until a complete security audit and credential rotation is performed.
